summary: Master LMS implementation, SCORM/xAPI standards, and digital learning strategy. 5-day hands-on course for L&D professionals. Enroll with TrainingCred today.
lede: LMS implementation is a strategic process for matching a learning platform to organizational needs and performance goals. For L&D and HR technology professionals, it covers assessing learning needs, defining requirements, and evaluating vendors before configuration and rollout. You’ll also practice content migration, user and enrollment setup, pilot testing, and using learner analytics to report on engagement and outcomes.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mid-career L&D and HR technology professionals who are directly involved in planning, selecting, implementing, or managing a digital learning platform. You should have at least one to two years of experience in a learning, training, or HR technology role. No software development or coding background is required, but comfort navigating web-based platforms and working with spreadsheet-based data is assumed.
audience: Organizational Development Analysts using LMS data
modules: Digital Learning Landscape and Strategic Foundations
Learning Needs Analysis and LMS Requirements Definition
LMS Configuration, Administration, and Compliance Workflows
Pilot Testing, Change Management, and Go-Live Planning
Learning Analytics, LRS Reporting, and Training ROI
LMS Strategy, Roadmap, and Stakeholder Reporting
prerequisites: This course is designed for intermediate-level professionals with at least one to two years of experience in an L&D, training, HR technology, or instructional design role. You should be comfortable navigating web-based platforms and working with spreadsheet tools for data analysis. No software development, coding, or database administration skills are required. Familiarity with basic eLearning concepts — such as what an LMS does, what SCORM is, and how online courses are structured — is assumed but not tested as a prerequisite. Participants who have never worked with an LMS before are advised to complete a self-paced LMS orientation module (provided as pre-reading) before Day 1. Participants should bring a laptop capable of running a modern web browser; all LMS sandbox environments, LRS tools, and content authoring previews are browser-based and require no software installation.
